source.title: Efficient Estimation of Influence of a Training Instance
source.authors: Sosuke Kobayashi; Sho Yokoi; Jun Suzuki; Kentaro Inui

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that adding instance-specific dropout can reduce validation accuracy or make training unstable, and that its effect varies by model and dataset size. This is a refinement of the claim that dropout can improve generalization in some regimes; it does not test the catalog's other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper tests turn-over dropout as an influence-estimation method and reports its side effects on validation accuracy. Its data-cleansing results concern a domain-shift test set, so they do not test same-distribution generalization or V8's removal-and-retraining comparison. It does not report the claim's training-versus-test error gap. Learning-curve descriptions and influence examples are not separate claim-version results.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 tests V6 by adding ordinary dropout to a VGGNet19 classifier already using turn-over dropout: accuracy increases from 86.2% to 91.3%. The instance-specific masking experiments primarily evaluate the side effects of an influence-estimation method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose efficient influence estimation using instance-specific masks, demonstrate applications to complex models and domain-shift data cleansing, and acknowledge performance deterioration and the need to investigate remedies.
record.recipe_differences: Uses instance-specific flipped dropout masks to estimate training-instance influence; this is not the standard dropout intervention in the original dropout study or the version's stated dropout comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported side effect differs with dataset size and model/application: the BERT accuracy change is negligible at N=20,000 versus a slight decrease at N=5,000; all-layer BERT without adapters is unstable; VGGNet19 accuracy declines when turn-over dropout is applied after layer 11, with partial recovery from original dropout.

fits_no_version.finding: Static instance-specific masking reduces BERT accuracy at N=5,000, has negligible impact at N=20,000, destabilizes all-layer BERT training, and reduces VGGNet accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Turn-over dropout's performance costs depend on dataset size, architecture, and mask placement.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing examples with the most negative estimated influence improves electronics-domain accuracy and loss after training on movie reviews.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Influence-based data cleansing can improve held-out performance under domain shift.

record.problems: The authors state they experimented with successful architectures only. The VGGNet accuracy passage does not specify the evaluation split. The cleansing result uses four runs and an explicit distributional shift; it does not establish same-distribution generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results tied to V1–V5, V7, or V8 were reported. The loss-curve discussion in Section 4.2 and influence examples in Figures 3–5 do not quantify a versioned claim outcome. Appendix E's self-influence result is described in the text but concerns self-influence, not one of the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Ordinary dropout on very small datasets, excessive ordinary dropout causing underfitting, fully connected classifier comparisons, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ability to rank generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing high-memorization examples compared with equally many random removals. Appendix A offers speculation about language modeling, without this experiment.

record.verdict_notes: The ordinary-dropout comparison in R5 is the direct evidence for V6. Turn-over dropout deliberately preserves instance-specific exclusions and should not be treated as equivalent to standard dropout regularization. States marked cannot_determine for unlinked rows concern the listed claim versions, not the readability of their reported numbers.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Standard dropout configurations on fully connected and convolutional classifiers; very small training sets; removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing retraining with random removals on same-distribution test data.

rows.subject: BERT-base classifiers (bert-base-cased) with adapter modules
rows.operation_detail: Turn-over dropout applied to adapter modules and output layers
rows.locator: Section 4.1, Side Effect on Model Performance
rows.note: Authors describe the decrease as slight.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but instance-specific static masks on BERT adapters do not test V6's ordinary dropout intervention in fully connected or convolutional classifiers.

rows.subject: BERT-base classifiers (bert-base-cased) with adapter modules
rows.operation_detail: Turn-over dropout applied to adapter modules and output layers
rows.locator: Section 4.1, Side Effect on Model Performance
rows.note: The paper calls the change negligible.
rows.check: The negligible accuracy change is correctly reported, but this static-mask BERT intervention does not establish ordinary dropout's effect under V6. A negligible change would not support a claim of reduced error.

rows.subject: BERT without adapter modules
rows.operation_detail: Turn-over dropout applied on all layers
rows.locator: Section 4.1, Side Effect on Model Performance
rows.note: The text does not give a corresponding accuracy value.
rows.check: Training instability under all-layer turn-over dropout does not measure held-out error and cannot establish a reversed V6 effect.

rows.subject: VGGNet19
rows.operation_detail: Turn-over dropout applied after the 11th layer
rows.locator: Section 4.1, Side Effect on Model Performance
rows.note: Authors say turn-over dropout allowed more overfitting than the baseline. The reported accuracies are not explicitly identified as validation or test in this passage.
rows.check: The intervention uses fixed instance-specific masks rather than ordinary dropout. Correct the application condition to all layers after layer 11. The setup identifies the 10,000 evaluation images as validation data.

rows.subject: VGGNet19
rows.operation_detail: Original dropout added as regularization alongside turn-over dropout
rows.locator: Section 4.1, Side Effect on Model Performance
rows.note: Accuracy recovers from the turn-over-dropout result but remains below the baseline value of 92.0%; passage does not explicitly identify accuracy split.
rows.check: Adding ordinary dropout raises accuracy from 86.2% to 91.3%, a clear reduction in held-out error. Remaining below the separate 92.0% baseline does not make this incremental dropout benefit partial. The setup identifies the evaluation split as validation.

relationships.condition: VGGNet19 on CIFAR-10, adding ordinary dropout alongside turn-over dropout
relationships.reason: R5 reports accuracy increasing from 86.2% to 91.3%, supporting a dropout benefit in this particular convolutional-classifier regime.
relationships.display_finding: Adding ordinary dropout reportedly increased test accuracy, but this comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Turn-over dropout on BERT SST-2 with 5,000 training instances and VGGNet19 on CIFAR-10
reader_labels.reason: Validation/accuracy declines under these settings (R1, R4); adding original dropout recovers some VGGNet accuracy but not to baseline (R5). The paper's intervention is turn-over dropout, so these results qualify the broader dropout claim.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors call the accuracy change negligible when applying turn-over dropout (R2), though this is a near-null side-effect finding rather than evidence of a test-error reduction.
